Osaka · food: Pair by area: Shinsekai + Chitose (Nishinari) + Tsutenkaku for a day. Chitose is shut Tue/Wed and Yaekatsu is shut Thu 24 Dec, so do it Fri 25. Tsuruhashi (Sora + Korea Town) is a daytime pairing; Korea Town stalls close by ~18:00. Minami: Marufuku/Kuromon morning, Wanaka snack, Kinryu as the 24h closer (w2). Fukushima (Homuraya ¥300 robata, Tottsuan) is the nearest izakaya strip to Kujō: Hanshin one stop to Nishikujō, then JR loop two stops. Tenma (Harukoma, Juggler to 3am) is the other crawl, also on the JR loop. Breakfast near base: Endo Sushi in the Central Wholesale Market (Noda) from 6:15, closed Sun and on market holidays, so check the 休市日 calendar for Tue 22/Wed 23. Christmas Eve/Day are normal business days in Japan; only date-night restaurants book out, izakaya and yakiniku are fine, but book Rikimaru/Tottsuan/Homuraya for 8 on the 24th and 25th. No year-end closures before the 26th. Counter shops (Yaekatsu, Harukoma, Daruma honten, Chitose) will split 8 into twos and threes; use Rikimaru, Tottsuan, Juggler and Homuraya to sit together. Transport: Hanshin Namba line runs from Kujō to Namba directly; an Osaka Metro 1-day Enjoy Eco Card pays off on Shinsekai/Tsuruhashi/Namba days.

Osaka · night: Base logic: Kujo (Nishi-ku) is 2 stops (~5 min) from Osaka-Namba on the Hanshin Namba line and on the Metro Chuo line via Hommachi, so Minami (Dotonbori, Ura-Namba, Amemura, Shinsaibashi) is home turf. A taxi from Namba is ~10–15 min, ~¥2,000 per car with the 20% late-night surcharge (split 4 ways); walking takes ~40 min. Pair the nights: (1) Mon 21: Tenma crawl from 17:30, then Shin-Umeda Shokudogai, then OWL Umeda (open nightly). (2) Minami nights: Hozenji, then Ura-Namba crawl, then Jankara, then Giraffe 22:00–04:00, then Round1 Sennichimae (24h) karaoke/Spo-Cha until the first train ~05:00. (3) Amemura night: Space Station, Triangle Park, then Circus (Thu–Sat only). Fukushima is the closest quality izakaya area to Kujo (taxi ~10 min). Kyoto (w3): do Pontocho at dusk and Kiyamachi bars after a Kyoto day, but leave Kawaramachi by ~23:00 to connect to Kujo (verify last trains on Jorudan); Kitsune Kyoto only works as an all-nighter with the first train back. Christmas: Thu 24 is a couples' date night (restaurants full, clubs run Xmas parties); Fri 25 = Christmas plus the weekend plus peak year-end bonenkai, so it is the biggest party night of the stay. Book Giraffe tickets ahead and reserve any izakaya for 8 that night. Rules: drinking/club age is 20+, carry original passports (clubs and Round1 check ID; under-18s barred 22:00–05:00 in Osaka). Many clubs refuse shorts/sandals and visible tattoos. Ignore street touts in Shinsaibashi/Dotonbori. Jankara stops serving alcohol at midnight. Budget: ¥1,500–3,000 per person for a standing-bar crawl, club entry ~¥1,000–3,500 incl. 1 drink, so a full night is ~¥5,000–8,000 each. Free Round1/Jankara app memberships cut prices (w10). Year-end: Dec 21–26 is before the New Year closures, so nightlife runs normally. CORRECTION: the osakatourism.org guide cited for Shin-Umeda Shokudogai and Space Station does not name them; treat both as single-signal (Google Maps) until re-checked.

Osaka · shop: Shopping logic. MINAMI DAY (the main shopping day, best a weekday, 21–24 Dec): Hanshin Namba line Kujō → Osaka-Namba (2 stops) ~10:30 → Den Den Town/Ota Road + Suruga-ya (open 10–11) → walk past Namba Parks → north up Shinsaibashi-suji (drugstores, Daimaru/Pokémon DX, PARCO) → west across Midosuji into Ame-mura (vintage opens ~12–13: Kinji/Big Step first, Triangle Park loop, Mandarake) → Horie Orange Street (JAM) → late Don Quijote Dotonbori after dinner (quiet after 21:00; PPIH says no refund fee). UMEDA HALF-DAY: LUCUA (Nintendo OSAKA 13F) → Grand Front only if time → Nakazakicho vintage from 13:00 → Hankyu/Hanshin depachika 18:00+ for markdowns and boxed souvenirs. KYOTO: Shinkyogoku/Teramachi + Nintendo KYOTO only as the last 60–90 min of a Kyoto day, then Hankyu Kyoto-Kawaramachi → Umeda direct. TIMING: vintage shops rarely open before noon, some close Wednesdays; 25 Dec (Fri) and 26 Dec (Sat) are the most crowded; winter sales start around 1–2 Jan, after Osaka. TAX-FREE (purchases from 1 Nov 2026, refund system): pay the full price incl. 10% tax; minimum ¥5,000 excl. tax per person, per store, per day, with each person's own passport (purchases can't be pooled); refund only after customs confirms export within 90 days, so it is done at Haneda T3 on 29 Dec at the customs kiosk BEFORE bag drop, with every tax-free item in hand (register Visit Japan Web to speed it up); if one item on a receipt is missing or used, the whole receipt loses the refund; snacks and cosmetics used in Japan don't qualify, so buy anything you'll eat or use on a separate receipt; refunds come from the shop or its refund operator (card, app, or airport cash), and fees vary by operator. Leave extra time at Haneda for the kiosk queue.

Osaka · sights: AREA LOGIC (Osaka base, Kujo; 21 Dec Mon to 26 Dec Sat 2026). Kujo is on both the Osaka Metro Chuo Line and the Hanshin Namba Line, which is unusually well connected for day trips: Hanshin through-trains run to Kintetsu-Nara with no change; 1 stop to Nishikujo then JR Yumesaki Line for USJ; 1 stop to Bentencho (Solaniwa onsen); 3 to Osakako (Kaiyukan). Suggested pairing: (1) USJ on Mon 21 or Tue 22; avoid 24–25 Dec, which are crowded and pricier, with school holidays starting. (2) Kyoto east day: Fushimi Inari at 06:30–07:00, then Keihan to Kiyomizu and Higashiyama by 08:30–09:00, Gion at midday. Keihan Kyoto-Osaka pass ¥1,650 vs ¥490 single from Yodoyabashi, so it only pays with 4+ rides. (3) Kyoto west day: Hankyu 1-Day ¥1,300 to Arashiyama by 07:30, then Kinkaku-ji at 09:00. Alternatively combine Arashiyama with Nara. (4) Nara half-day by Hanshin/Kintetsu: deer and Todai-ji 08:30–13:00, back for an Osaka evening. (5) Osaka Amazing Pass day (¥3,500 1-day / ¥5,000 2-day): Osaka Castle and Gozabune in the morning, Umeda Sky before 15:00 (pass entry cutoff), Tsutenkaku, then the Tombori cruise at night. It pays for itself with 3 or more paid sights. Christmas lights: Hikari Renaissance (Nakanoshima, 11–25 Dec, so it ends Christmas night) plus Midosuji Illumination (to 31 Dec, lit until 01:00) make one free evening walk from Yodoyabashi to Namba that ends in Dotonbori for nightlife (w2). Umeda Sky Christmas runs to 25 Dec. KOBE LUMINARIE is NOT on in December: since 2024 it moved to late Jan/early Feb (2026 edition was 30 Jan–8 Feb), so skip Kobe for lights. Arashiyama Hanatouro ended in 2021, and the Osaka Castle Illuminage 2026–27 dates are not yet announced (2025–26 ran 1 Nov–1 Feb, ¥2,000). PASSES: the JR paper Kansai Area Pass stopped selling on 30 Sep 2026. The WEST QR version is sold only by agencies outside Japan, so buy before flying if you want it, though it's rarely worth it from Kujo, which is a private-railway base. The KANSAI RAILWAY PASS (2-day ¥5,600, non-consecutive days) usually does NOT beat ICOCA for one Kyoto day plus one Nara day from Kujo. Default to ICOCA plus single-company day passes (Hankyu ¥1,300, Kintetsu 1-day ¥1,900 only if you do Nara and Kyoto on Kintetsu the same day). Onsen: Spa World and many sento refuse tattoos, including stickers. Spa World adds ¥1,300 after midnight. Year-end: Osaka Castle closes 28 Dec, which is after this leg, so not a problem.

Tokyo · food: Area logic. Stay 1 (15–19 Dec, Ninja House, Toshima): Ikebukuro East exit is the food base; Mutekiya (to 4am) and Kinsuien/Mugendo AYCE yakiniku are all within about 5 min of each other. The first-night dinner after the Haneda 15:00 landing is easy there (Keikyu + Yamanote/Marunouchi to Ikebukuro, about 60–70 min). Do Tsukiji (breakfast) + Tsukishima monja (dinner) + Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai/teamLab as one east-side day: all on the Oedo/Yurikamome lines. Best on Thu 17 or Fri 18 Dec; Wed 16 may be a market holiday. Stay 2 (26–29 Dec, Garfield House, Shinjuku): breakfast at Shinpachi Shokudo (7:00), Fuunji tsukemen at opening, Tsunahachi tempura (book TableCheck), Uobei and Isomaru 24h for late nights. Ameyoko is on the Yamanote from Shinjuku/Ikebukuro: go 26–28 Dec mornings, avoid 30–31. Year-end traps: Sun 27 Dec, the Tsukiji market and many shops are shut; independent shops (Fuunji, Kondo monja) take year-end breaks from about 29–31 Dec; Mutekiya and Kondo close 31 Dec–3 Jan (after the trip). Chains (Isomaru, Uobei, Shinpachi) are the safe bets on 28–29 Dec. Budget: AYCE yakiniku with drinks (¥2,000–7,600) and monja are the best-value group feasts; book Kinsuien, Moheji and Tsunahachi for 8 two to three weeks ahead. Departure 29 Dec: eat at Haneda T3 Edo Koji before security, since 29 Dec is a peak travel day.

Tokyo · night: Two bases set the night logic. NIGHTS 15–18 DEC (Ninja House, Toshima): stay local on Tue 15 (arrival) and Wed 16. Daitokai (24h, beer about ¥250) and Wakadaisho by the West and North Exits, then Round1 Ikebukuro (24h bowling, karaoke and arcade) or Big Echo West Exit (until 06:00 on Fri and Sat); all within walking distance of the stay. Thu 17: Shibuya or Ebisu (Ebisu Yokocho, Shibuya Yokocho). FRI 18 DEC is the big night and peak year-end office party (bōnenkai) season, so izakaya fill early: book any sit-down for 8. Headline: ZEROTOKYO Steve Angello (buy advance tickets). Take taxis or wait for the first trains back to Toshima, and keep the 19 Dec Hakone departure in mind. NIGHTS 26–28 DEC (Garfield House, Shinjuku): everything is walkable. Sat 26: Omoide Yokocho, then Kabuki Hall (seats 8 walk-in), then ZEROTOKYO NEON STARS, then Nagi ramen (24h). Sun 27 and Mon 28: ZEROTOKYO (Mon–Wed per Google) and WOMB (Sun/Mon) are closed, so do Umi no Ie unlimited nomihodai (¥1,480) and Golden Gai in groups of 4, then ATOM Shibuya (open nightly, men ¥900 before 23:30) or Karaokekan Kabukicho (until 06:00). YEAR-END: chains, clubs, karaoke and Round1 run normally through 28 Dec; small Golden Gai and Omoide stalls may start closing from about 29 Dec. Mon 28 is the last safe night. The flight is 17:20 on 29 Dec, so leave Shinjuku by about 14:00. ID: every club is strictly 20+ and wants the ORIGINAL passport (no photos or copies); no sandals, tank tops or sports pants. Last trains run about 00:00–00:30, so plan to party until the first train (about 05:00) or split taxis.

Tokyo · shop: AREA LOGIC (Tokyo shopping). Stay 1, 15–19 Dec, Ninja House/Ikebukuro: arrival evening = animate flagship, Otome Road, Sunshine City/Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo, then the Ikebukuro Donki. Do an east-side day: Akihabara (Mandarake Complex, Radio Kaikan, Super Potato) + Ueno Ameyoko/mita sneakers, 2 Yamanote stops apart. Do Ameyoko in this first stay, because from 28 Dec it becomes a New Year food-market crush. Do Tokyo Station souvenirs (Character Street/Okashi Land) here too, if they fit. Stay 2, 26–29 Dec, Garfield House/Shinjuku: West day = Koenji (from 12:00) → Nakano Broadway, both on the Chuo line 6 min from Shinjuku. South day = Takeshita at 10:00 → Ura-Hara → Cat Street on foot → Shibuya PARCO/Miyashita Park; or Shimokitazawa 12:00–17:00 → Inokashira line 4 min → Shibuya, then MEGA Donki late. Nakameguro/Daikanyama is optional and low value for this budget. The Yamanote and Chuo lines cover all of it, so use IC cards (Suica/PASMO), no pass needed. YEAR-END: department stores and malls should keep normal hours 26–30 Dec (31 Dec shortened, 1 Jan closed). But the big winter sales and 初売り start 2 Jan (Isetan, Lumine) or 3 Jan (PARCO Grand Bazaar), after the 29 Dec flight, so malls are full price. Get value from secondhand (Koenji, NY Joe, 2nd Street, Mandarake) and Donki instead. Depachika are packed on 28–30 Dec with osechi shoppers. Some small vintage shops close irregularly around New Year, so check their Instagram. TAX-FREE (from 1 Nov 2026): pay full price incl. 10% tax, show your passport, and register the refund method. Keep ≥¥5,000 ex-tax on one receipt per shop per day, per person. Don't eat or use what you'll claim, and keep the whole receipt's items together. At Haneda T3 on 29 Dec, do the customs kiosk (or Visit Japan Web on airport Wi-Fi) with all goods BEFORE bag drop. Arrive by ~14:00 for the 17:20 flight on this peak departure day. Donki waives the refund fee unless you take cash at the airport.

Tokyo · sights: Leg 1 (Ninja House, Ikebukuro, 15–18 Dec) is the window for everything Christmas: Roppongi Hills, the Shiba Park and Shin-Toyosu Christmas markets and the illuminations all END 25 Dec, so none are left on leg 2. Pairings: (a) Roppongi Hills Keyakizaka then Shiba Park market under Tokyo Tower (walk or Oedo line, one evening); (b) teamLab Planets (8:00 or 15:00 slot), then the Shin-Toyosu market, then Manyo Club onsen, all within 5 min on the Yurikamome line. Time-locked leg-1 events: Setagaya Boro-ichi 15–16 Dec (go 16th, 9:00); Asakusa Hagoita-ichi 17–19 Dec (go 17/18 at dusk; Senso-ji at 6:30 to beat crowds). Kawagoe is the cheap half-day from Ikebukuro (¥490 each way). Leg 2 (Garfield House, Shinjuku, 26–29 Dec): Odaiba Rainbow Fireworks Sat 26 Dec at 19:00 (free); Tokyo Government deck free on 26/27 only (north deck closed 28th, both closed 29–31 Dec); Kamakura/Enoshima on 27 or 28 Dec with the ¥1,640 Odakyu Freepass; Ameyoko year-end market on 27/28 Dec; Thermae-yu in Kabukicho for late soaks and the last-morning shower before the 17:20 flight. Year-end (年末年始): museums and gardens mostly close from 28/29 Dec (Imperial East Gardens 28 Dec – 3 Jan); temples, Shibuya Sky, teamLab and onsen stay open. Booking calendar: KKday Christmas-market tickets now (weekday ¥1,000, includes mug); Ghibli Museum December tickets go on sale 10 Nov at 10:00 JST on Lawson Ticket (QR system from Nov 2026, ¥110 fee; closed Tuesdays, so not 15 or 29 Dec); Shibuya Sky sunset slot (about 15:40) the minute sales open, 2–4 weeks ahead (check in mid-Nov); teamLab Planets weekday early slot about 3 weeks ahead. Optional for anime fans: Comiket C109 runs 29–31 Dec at Tokyo Big Sight, but only a morning on 29 Dec fits before a 17:20 Haneda flight. Transport: a Tokyo Subway Ticket (24/48/72h) covers Metro and Toei (Roppongi, Shiba, Asakusa, Ueno) but not the Yurikamome, JR, Seibu, Tobu or Odakyu. Skip Skytree and Tokyo Tower decks: Shibuya Sky plus the free Tokyo Government deck cover the views.

Tokyo · food: I've saved 14 places for Tokyo, Dec 15–19. Each has at least two independent sources, mostly from 2026. The biggest thing to act on now: **Friday Dec 18 is forecast to be Japan's busiest night of the year for year-end work parties (bōnenkai).** A Japanese restaurant-industry forecast puts it at over 4× a normal night, so book anything for that Friday now.

**Near Ninja House (Ikebukuro)**
- **Mutekiya** – Ikebukuro's famous rich tonkotsu ramen, open until 4am. Best eaten after midnight, when the queue is shortest.
- **Kan7 Tosakko** – a ramen shop open until 5am, for when Mutekiya's line is too long.
- **Nemuro Hanamaru** – the Hokkaido conveyor-sushi chain that has 1–3 hour waits at Tokyo Station. It opened inside Ikebukuro station in June 2026. There are no bookings: take a ticket from the machine, then shop nearby until it calls you on LINE.
- **Kingyuen** – all-you-can-eat wagyu yakiniku with private rooms for 6–8. Courses start at about ¥3,190 per person. Book online 3–4 weeks ahead.
- **Onigiri Bongo** (Otsuka, one stop away) – Tokyo's most famous rice-ball shop. Weekday waits are 1–2.5 hours, so phone a takeaway order the day before (03-3910-5617). Closed Sundays, and listed hours conflict between sites, so check Google Maps the night before.

**Food streets and group meals**
- **Tsukiji Outer Market** – breakfast grazing, best 8:00–10:30. **Don't go Wednesday Dec 16**: Wednesdays are usually market holidays and many stalls are shut. Skip Toyosu's Senkyaku Banrai food hall; reviews say it isn't worth it.
- **Tsukishima monja at Moheji** – monjayaki is Tokyo's own hot-plate dish, and it's the best group meal on the list. Book a table for 8 (two hot plates). It's 15 minutes from Tsukiji, so do both the same day.
- **Ameyoko (Ueno)** – the cheapest drinking street in town, with day drinking from 10am. At Daitoryo, expect to be split 4+4. Some foreign visitors in 2024–25 complained on Xiaohongshu that they were seated more slowly, so treat it as a bar-hop and move on if the wait is long.
- **Fuunji** – Tokyo's benchmark tsukemen (dipping ramen). Closed Sundays, which doesn't affect your dates.

**Shinjuku nights**
- **Izakaya Umi no Ie** – ¥1,480 for up to 7 hours of all-you-can-drink, including free gyoza and oden. You need the Hot Pepper coupon, and it's open until 5am.
- **Shinjuku Mugen Gyoza** – 2 hours of gyoza plus drinks for ¥2,750 if you arrive before 18:00. It has private rooms.
- **Kabuki Hall** – a food hall open until 5am with DJs and big shared tables, so all 8 can sit together.
- **Omoide Yokocho** – most stalls can't fit 8 walk-ins. Book Torien instead (opens 13:00) and go 15:00–17:00, before the evening rush.
- **Ebisu Yokocho** – late-night alley bars, better than Shibuya Yokocho, which has mixed reviews.

**How to plan the days**
- **Pairings:**
  - Tsukiji in the morning, then Tsukishima monja, then Ginza.
  - Ueno/Ameyoko with Akihabara.
  - Shibuya shopping, then Ebisu Yokocho.
  - Kabukicho nights with an early-bird dinner first.
  - Every night ends with ramen in Ikebukuro: from Shinjuku it's 5 minutes on the JR Yamanote line.
- **Getting home:** last trains leave around 00:30. A taxi from Kabukicho to Toshima is roughly ¥3,000–4,000, about ¥500 each split four ways.
- **Saving money:** a Tokyo Subway Ticket (72h is about ¥1,500) covers Tsukiji, Tsukishima, Ueno and Shinjuku-sanchome. The Yamanote line isn't included, so use a Suica card for that. Book izakayas through Hot Pepper Gourmet: you get the cheap coupons and earn points.
- **Booking timing:** book Kingyuen, Moheji and the Friday plans 3+ weeks out. Tue–Thu nights are much easier. Queue-only places (Bongo, Fuunji, Mutekiya) work best right at opening or after midnight.

Hakone · food-night: I've saved 9 places for Hakone (19–21 Dec). Hakone is a hot-spring town with very little nightlife, so the plan is two booked nights out near the villa, drinks at the villa, and Round1 and clubs saved for Osaka and Tokyo.

**The two nights out:**
- **Saturday 19 Dec:** dinner at **Hakone Sushi** at 17:00. It's in Sengokuhara, close to the villa, and Google reviews say it's full even on weekdays, so phone to book the tatami room for 8. Then go to **MONTA**, an izakaya-bar open until midnight. Reviews mention groups of 8 who booked ahead and a free pickup for guests staying nearby; ask about the pickup when you call.
- **Sunday 20 Dec:** MONTA and Hakone Sushi are both closed Sundays. Go to **Gora Brewery & Grill** (craft beer, closes around 21:00), then take a 15-minute taxi to **Funny's**, an American burger bar in Miyanoshita that's open late. Funny's is small, so phone ahead for 8.

**Getting around and timing:**
- Buses into Sengokuhara stop early in the evening, so plan on taxis at night. Two taxis carry the 8 of you.
- **Monday 21 Dec** is the worst day for food: MONTA, Hakone Sushi and Funny's are all closed. Leave in the morning and have lunch at **Odawara Minato Shokudo**, a seafood place one minute from Odawara Station that's open daily 11:00–21:00. Then catch the shinkansen from Odawara.
- **Lunches:** for **Tamura Ginkatsutei**'s fried tofu-and-pork dish in Gora, get a numbered ticket around 10:30 on the weekend (waits run 30–60 minutes, cash or PayPay only). **Hatsuhana Soba** in Yumoto is a quick lunch on arrival or departure day.
- **Splurge:** **Itoh Dining by Nobu** in Gora does wagyu cooked in front of you. Lunch costs much less than dinner, but book 2–4 weeks ahead and you may be split 4+4 at the counter. I didn't confirm its map pin or Hatsuhana's.

**Ways to save money:**
- The **Hakone Freepass**, bought before the trip, covers most local buses, trains, the ropeway and the lake boat. Your sights researcher is covering it.
- Buy drinks before you go up the mountain. The A Coop supermarket in Sengokuhara closes at 18:00, so shop on the way in, or stock up in Odawara or at the MaxValu in Gotemba. Drinking at the villa's hot spring is your cheapest night.

**Round1:** I found no Round1 in Odawara, and Hakone has nothing like it. Do Round1 in Osaka or Tokyo.

Hakone · sights-shop: I've saved 12 candidates for Hakone, 19–21 Dec. Two things change your plan:

- **Part of the ropeway is closed on your dates.** The Sounzan–Owakudani section is shut 7–24 Dec 2026 for maintenance. From Sengokuhara you don't need it: take the bus to Togendai, ride up to Owakudani and back, then take the pirate ship.
- **Sat 19 Dec is a geisha night in Hakone-Yumoto.** The "Furatto Geisha" event runs on the 1st and 3rd Saturday of each month, and the 19th is the 3rd. Three geisha dance, then you play drinking games with them, at 18:30 or 20:00. No booking needed; it was about ¥3,000 including a drink in 2025.

**Suggested days**
- **Sat 19:**
  - Take the Romancecar train from Shinjuku to Hakone-Yumoto. Book seats as soon as they open a month ahead, because 8 seats together on a December Saturday sell out.
  - In the afternoon, go to Hakone Yuryo. It's a day onsen where tattoos are OK and you can book private open-air baths for 2 hours, so the whole group can soak together. Book a couple of the large rooms.
  - Do souvenir shopping on the Yumoto station street before about 17:30, when shops start closing.
  - Go to the 18:30 geisha show, then take the bus up to Sengokuhara. I didn't check the last bus time, so look it up. If you miss it, you'll need taxis.
- **Sun 20:**
  - Take the first ropeway car (about 9:00) from Togendai to Owakudani for the sulphur vents, black eggs and clearest Fuji views.
  - Ride the pirate ship to Motohakone and see the lakeside torii at Hakone Shrine. By midday the queue for the torii photo can be long, so take your shot from the side path instead.
  - From about 16:00, see the Christmas crystal lights at Hakone Glass no Mori, which is near your villa. Candles are lit 1–25 Dec, and it closes at 17:30.
  - The Open-Air Museum (outdoor sculpture park) is quiet after 15:30, so it fits on Sunday afternoon or Monday morning.
- **Mon 21:**
  - Get to Gotemba Premium Outlets for the 10:00 opening; weekdays are much quieter. It has about 290 stores (Nike, New Balance, Beams and others), and the official app has coupons. There's a direct bus from Sengoku.
  - At dusk, go to the Tokinosumika illumination (on until 7 Mar 2027), which has a craft brewery on site. Both are on the Hakone Tozan bus line from Sengoku.
  - If you're heading to Osaka next, Gotemba connects to the bullet train at Mishima. I haven't checked buses or times for that link.

**Money and passes**
- Buy the 3-day Hakone Freepass: ¥7,500 from Shinjuku or ¥6,400 from Odawara (prices since Oct 2025). It covers the trains, ropeway, pirate ship and most buses, and the ropeway plus ship loop alone uses up much of the value.
- Buy it on Odakyu's EMot app to skip the counter queue. The Romancecar seat costs extra.
- Bring passports to the outlets for tax-free shopping. From what I know (I didn't confirm it here), Japan switches to a refund system from 1 Nov 2026. You'd pay the tax in the shop and get it back at the airport, showing the goods, so keep receipts and don't open purchases.

**Gaps and traps**
- **Nightlife:** Hakone basically has none apart from the geisha night and Tokinosumika's beer hall. Treat these as your onsen-and-scenery days and do the big nights out in Tokyo and Osaka.
- **Round1:** Hakone has no Round1; the nearest is in Hiratsuka, more than an hour away. Do it in Tokyo or Osaka.
- **Weekend crowds:** do the ropeway and pirate ship loop early on Sunday and go shopping on Monday, not at the weekend.
- **Daylight:** it gets dark around 16:30, and the ropeway and ships stop around 16:00–16:15. Plan the outdoor sights for mornings and put the lights, onsen and drinking after dark.

- Buy drinks before you go up the mountain. The A Coop supermarket in Sengokuhara closes at 18:00, so shop on the way in, or stock up in Odawara or at the MaxValu in Gotemba. Drinking at the villa's hot spring is your cheapest night.

**Round1:** I found no Round1 in Odawara, and Hakone has nothing like it. Do Round1 in Osaka or Tokyo.

Tokyo · food: I've saved 14 places for Tokyo, Dec 15–19. Each has at least two independent sources, mostly from 2026. The biggest thing to act on now: **Friday Dec 18 is forecast to be Japan's busiest night of the year for year-end work parties (bōnenkai).** A Japanese restaurant-industry forecast puts it at over 4× a normal night, so book anything for that Friday now.

**Near Ninja House (Ikebukuro)**
- **Mutekiya** – Ikebukuro's famous rich tonkotsu ramen, open until 4am. Best eaten after midnight, when the queue is shortest.
- **Kan7 Tosakko** – a ramen shop open until 5am, for when Mutekiya's line is too long.
- **Nemuro Hanamaru** – the Hokkaido conveyor-sushi chain that has 1–3 hour waits at Tokyo Station. It opened inside Ikebukuro station in June 2026. There are no bookings: take a ticket from the machine, then shop nearby until it calls you on LINE.
- **Kingyuen** – all-you-can-eat wagyu yakiniku with private rooms for 6–8. Courses start at about ¥3,190 per person. Book online 3–4 weeks ahead.
- **Onigiri Bongo** (Otsuka, one stop away) – Tokyo's most famous rice-ball shop. Weekday waits are 1–2.5 hours, so phone a takeaway order the day before (03-3910-5617). Closed Sundays, and listed hours conflict between sites, so check Google Maps the night before.

**Food streets and group meals**
- **Tsukiji Outer Market** – breakfast grazing, best 8:00–10:30. **Don't go Wednesday Dec 16**: Wednesdays are usually market holidays and many stalls are shut. Skip Toyosu's Senkyaku Banrai food hall; reviews say it isn't worth it.
- **Tsukishima monja at Moheji** – monjayaki is Tokyo's own hot-plate dish, and it's the best group meal on the list. Book a table for 8 (two hot plates). It's 15 minutes from Tsukiji, so do both the same day.
- **Ameyoko (Ueno)** – the cheapest drinking street in town, with day drinking from 10am. At Daitoryo, expect to be split 4+4. Some foreign visitors in 2024–25 complained on Xiaohongshu that they were seated more slowly, so treat it as a bar-hop and move on if the wait is long.
- **Fuunji** – Tokyo's benchmark tsukemen (dipping ramen). Closed Sundays, which doesn't affect your dates.

**Shinjuku nights**
- **Izakaya Umi no Ie** – ¥1,480 for up to 7 hours of all-you-can-drink, including free gyoza and oden. You need the Hot Pepper coupon, and it's open until 5am.
- **Shinjuku Mugen Gyoza** – 2 hours of gyoza plus drinks for ¥2,750 if you arrive before 18:00. It has private rooms.
- **Kabuki Hall** – a food hall open until 5am with DJs and big shared tables, so all 8 can sit together.
- **Omoide Yokocho** – most stalls can't fit 8 walk-ins. Book Torien instead (opens 13:00) and go 15:00–17:00, before the evening rush.
- **Ebisu Yokocho** – late-night alley bars, better than Shibuya Yokocho, which has mixed reviews.

**How to plan the days**
- **Pairings:**
  - Tsukiji in the morning, then Tsukishima monja, then Ginza.
  - Ueno/Ameyoko with Akihabara.
  - Shibuya shopping, then Ebisu Yokocho.
  - Kabukicho nights with an early-bird dinner first.
  - Every night ends with ramen in Ikebukuro: from Shinjuku it's 5 minutes on the JR Yamanote line.
- **Getting home:** last trains leave around 00:30. A taxi from Kabukicho to Toshima is roughly ¥3,000–4,000, about ¥500 each split four ways.
- **Saving money:** a Tokyo Subway Ticket (72h is about ¥1,500) covers Tsukiji, Tsukishima, Ueno and Shinjuku-sanchome. The Yamanote line isn't included, so use a Suica card for that. Book izakayas through Hot Pepper Gourmet: you get the cheap coupons and earn points.
- **Booking timing:** book Kingyuen, Moheji and the Friday plans 3+ weeks out. Tue–Thu nights are much easier. Queue-only places (Bongo, Fuunji, Mutekiya) work best right at opening or after midnight.

Hakone · sights-shop: I've saved 12 candidates for Hakone, 19–21 Dec. Two things change your plan:

- **Part of the ropeway is closed on your dates.** The Sounzan–Owakudani section is shut 7–24 Dec 2026 for maintenance. From Sengokuhara you don't need it: take the bus to Togendai, ride up to Owakudani and back, then take the pirate ship.
- **Sat 19 Dec is a geisha night in Hakone-Yumoto.** The "Furatto Geisha" event runs on the 1st and 3rd Saturday of each month, and the 19th is the 3rd. Three geisha dance, then you play drinking games with them, at 18:30 or 20:00. No booking needed; it was about ¥3,000 including a drink in 2025.

**Suggested days**
- **Sat 19:**
  - Take the Romancecar train from Shinjuku to Hakone-Yumoto. Book seats as soon as they open a month ahead, because 8 seats together on a December Saturday sell out.
  - In the afternoon, go to Hakone Yuryo. It's a day onsen where tattoos are OK and you can book private open-air baths for 2 hours, so the whole group can soak together. Book a couple of the large rooms.
  - Do souvenir shopping on the Yumoto station street before about 17:30, when shops start closing.
  - Go to the 18:30 geisha show, then take the bus up to Sengokuhara. I didn't check the last bus time, so look it up. If you miss it, you'll need taxis.
- **Sun 20:**
  - Take the first ropeway car (about 9:00) from Togendai to Owakudani for the sulphur vents, black eggs and clearest Fuji views.
  - Ride the pirate ship to Motohakone and see the lakeside torii at Hakone Shrine. By midday the queue for the torii photo can be long, so take your shot from the side path instead.
  - From about 16:00, see the Christmas crystal lights at Hakone Glass no Mori, which is near your villa. Candles are lit 1–25 Dec, and it closes at 17:30.
  - The Open-Air Museum (outdoor sculpture park) is quiet after 15:30, so it fits on Sunday afternoon or Monday morning.
- **Mon 21:**
  - Get to Gotemba Premium Outlets for the 10:00 opening; weekdays are much quieter. It has about 290 stores (Nike, New Balance, Beams and others), and the official app has coupons. There's a direct bus from Sengoku.
  - At dusk, go to the Tokinosumika illumination (on until 7 Mar 2027), which has a craft brewery on site. Both are on the Hakone Tozan bus line from Sengoku.
  - If you're heading to Osaka next, Gotemba connects to the bullet train at Mishima. I haven't checked buses or times for that link.

**Money and passes**
- Buy the 3-day Hakone Freepass: ¥7,500 from Shinjuku or ¥6,400 from Odawara (prices since Oct 2025). It covers the trains, ropeway, pirate ship and most buses, and the ropeway plus ship loop alone uses up much of the value.
- Buy it on Odakyu's EMot app to skip the counter queue. The Romancecar seat costs extra.
- Bring passports to the outlets for tax-free shopping. From what I know (I didn't confirm it here), Japan switches to a refund system from 1 Nov 2026. You'd pay the tax in the shop and get it back at the airport, showing the goods, so keep receipts and don't open purchases.

**Gaps and traps**
- **Nightlife:** Hakone basically has none apart from the geisha night and Tokinosumika's beer hall. Treat these as your onsen-and-scenery days and do the big nights out in Tokyo and Osaka.
- **Round1:** Hakone has no Round1; the nearest is in Hiratsuka, more than an hour away. Do it in Tokyo or Osaka.
- **Weekend crowds:** do the ropeway and pirate ship loop early on Sunday and go shopping on Monday, not at the weekend.
- **Daylight:** it gets dark around 16:30, and the ropeway and ships stop around 16:00–16:15. Plan the outdoor sights for mornings and put the lights, onsen and drinking after dark.

Hakone · food: I've saved **18 food and drink places** for Hakone, Dec 19–21. Your dates are Saturday to Monday, so very few of them have their weekly closing day during your stay (most close on Wednesday or Thursday). Hours and some prices come from listings and posts; confirm by phone near the date. Almost everything needs a phone call in Japanese, so get your villa host or a Japanese speaker to make the bookings.

**The main problem: Sengokuhara goes dark early.** Most places shut by 20:30–21:00, and the only supermarket (A-Coop) closes at 18:00 and sells out. Hakone-Yumoto is the only area with real late-night bars, about 25–30 minutes away by taxi. So plan each night as dinner out, then either a bar that drives you back or drinking at the villa.

**Suggested plan:**
- **Sat 19, arrival:** Lunch at Odawara's fishing port. Aburiya is an 80-minute all-you-can-eat seafood barbecue, built for groups and all over Japanese TikTok this year. Do the big grocery and drinks shop at Odakyu OX in Odawara station (open to 21:00) before heading up. Dinner at **Hakone Kayaka**: big portions, private rooms and the best group izakaya in Sengokuhara. Then **Snack Takachan**, a karaoke bar open until 2am that can collect you from the villa if you arrange it.
- **Sun 20, Gora/Owakudani day:** Lunch at **Gyoza Center** (cheap, queues) or **Tamura Ginkatsutei** for tofu katsu, Hakone's one real local dish. Late afternoon at **Gora Brewery & Grill**, Hakone's own brewpub. Dinner either at **OHANA**, which picks you up and drives you home, or at **Shamoji** for sake (small; you may need to split 4+4).
- **Mon 21, leaving:** Cheap, huge plates at **Inakaya Daichi** by the Sengoku bus stop, or the fancier castle-style **Albergo Bamboo** (upstairs private room for about 9). If you'd rather eat on the way out, Odawara port is on your route: Warabe Saigyodo does good seafood bowls.

**Ways to save money:**
- **Rent a keg instead of paying bar prices.** Order a beer server and keg from **Yamakawaya**, a Sengokuhara liquor shop that sells its own Hakone craft beer. Do it 1–2 weeks ahead and pick it up on arrival.
- **Buy the Hakone Freepass** if you're doing the sightseeing loop. It covers the buses up to Sengokuhara, the mountain train, cable car, ropeway and lake boat. Check current prices on Odakyu's site.
- **Cook breakfast at the villa** from the Odawara shop. Breakfast cafés out in Sengokuhara aren't worth the trip.

**Book in late November:**
- Kayaka for Saturday
- Gora Brewery for Sunday
- OHANA, including the pick-up for 8
- Albergo Bamboo's private room, if you want it
- Aburiya

**Timing traps:**
- **Getting home from a night out:** If you go out in Hakone-Yumoto (Izakaya Hakoneji until midnight, then Flying Chicken until 2am), book a jumbo taxi or two taxis home. Expect roughly ¥7,000–9,000 per car. I couldn't confirm last-bus times from Yumoto to Sengokuhara; assume buses stop around 21:00.
- **Weekend queues:** Gyoza Center and Ginkatsutei have long weekend lines, so arrive at opening.
- **Unconfirmed details:** I don't have a closing day or opening times for OHANA or Hakone Sushi. Check when you call.

**Not worth it:** Skipping the food at Owakudani (the volcanic valley) loses you nothing; the famous black eggs are the only thing to eat there. Don't plan dinner around Gora either; it's quieter than Yumoto at night.
